summary: Ryosho Hayashi (1927–2008) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Taisho and Tokyo Metropolitan universities, taught at Tokyo Metropolitan Komatsugawa High School, and served at Taisho University as professor, dean, and professor emeritus.

Ryosho Nakamura (b. 1927) specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the Seventh Higher School, Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, and Rissho University. He was a professor at Kagoshima International University from circa 1968 to 1998.

Ryosho Tanaka (1933–2016) was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at and served Komazawa University in roles including professor, dean, museum director, and president. He also held posts at Ryukoku University, the Museum of Zen Culture and History, and Soto Zen Research Center.

Ryoshu Kouda works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Seitatsu Matsunami. Kouda held researcher posts at Taisho University (attested 1998) and Hasegawa Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 2006), and served on the Matsunami Seiren Sensei Koki Kinenkai secretariat.

Ryoshu Michihata (1903–1993) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Otani University (~1925–1928), where he later held a post (~1946–1969), and served as a professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University (~1969–1979).
Ryoshu Misaki (1921–2010) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University from circa 1942 to 1947 and later served there as professor emeritus from circa 1966 to 1992.

Ryoshun Okubo (b. 1954) studied at Waseda University, later serving there as Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism (~2004–2024). He also held posts with Taimon Kenkyūkai, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Ryosuke Furui (b. 1971) specializes in Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD from Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2007 and was appointed professor at the University of Tokyo in 2020.

Ryota Nakamura is a Buddhist studies researcher who pursued doctoral studies and held a graduate student researcher post at Toyo University (attested 2015). In the same year, he also served as a researcher at the Shinran Buddhist Center.
Ryotai Shibuya was a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed his education at Tendai Sect University and Kokugakuin University.
Ryoun Yamada (b. 1940) studied at Harvard Business School and worked in the financial and corporate sectors before becoming the leader of Sanbo Zen in 2004.

Ryudo Fujii is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson. He held posts with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (2003), Kokushikan University (2010), and Kyoto Women's University (2015).
Ryudo Suita is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Bukkyo University, attested between 1997 and 2010, and held a post there attested in 2020.

Ryugen Taga (b. 1931) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1950–1955). He served there as lecturer (~1957–1966), associate professor (~1966–1974), professor (~1974–2002), and president (~1992–1995).

Ryugen Tanemura (b. 1970) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. His academic posts include faculty at Taisho University (attested 2014–2026), researcher at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014), and lecturer at Nishogakusha University (attested 2013).

Ryuichi Abe (b. 1954) studied at Keio, SAIS/Johns Hopkins, and Columbia universities. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religion, he served as an associate professor at Columbia before becoming a professor of Japanese religions at Harvard University circa 2003.

Ryujo Yamada (1895–1974) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, studying under Sylvain Lévi. He contributed regularly to Hōbōgirin, served as professor and professor emeritus at Tohoku University, and was president at Musashino University.

Ryuken Nawa works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, he holds lecturer positions at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Ryuken Sato (1930–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar. In 2014, he is attested as professor emeritus at Taisho University and as an advisor at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute.
Ryuo (1856–1926) was a scholar of Buddhist studies who held teaching posts at To-ji and Koyasan University.
